findings.title: sim/cuda_reduction.py has ZERO test coverage despite being used by the PCG pressure solver
findings.description: This 175-line module performs CUDA JIT compilation via ctypes (build.build_cuda, build.load_cuda), manages a module-level mutable cache dict (_MODULES = {} at line 49), writes/reads .cu and .cubin files to disk (lines 62-100), and exposes CudaDotProduct.launch() which does raw pointer arithmetic via ctypes (lines 115-135). It is imported by pressure.py line 1487 ('from .cuda_reduction import CudaDotProduct') and instantiated at pressure.py:1489 ('self._pcg_dot = CudaDotProduct(self.device)'). No test file in tests/ imports or references cuda_reduction, CudaDotProduct, or _load_kernel. The error paths (compile failure at line 87-99, kernel load failure after 2 retries at line 101, launch failure at line 133) are entirely untested. The _MODULES global cache is never validated for stale entries or device lifecycle.
findings.impact: The PCG pressure solver's inner-product reduction -- a numerically critical operation in the conjugate gradient loop -- runs through this untested CUDA JIT path. A silent numerical error, stale cache entry, or file I/O failure would corrupt simulation results with no test to catch it.
findings.fix: Add unit tests for _load_kernel (mock warp build.load_cuda to simulate compile failure, stale cubin, and successful load), CudaDotProduct.__init__ (non-CUDA device rejection, module caching behavior), and CudaDotProduct.launch (launch result code != 0 path). Add a numerical correctness test comparing against wp.utils.array_inner on known vectors.

findings.title: Assertions run at module import time, not inside test functions -- will fail during pytest collection not as test results
findings.description: test_kernel_coverage.py has ZERO 'def test_*' functions (confirmed: grep returns no matches). The assertions at lines 41 ('assert lookup("paradigmAdvectParticles") is lookup("fluidSimAdvectParticles")'), 61 ('assert not missing'), and 62 ('assert not invalid_entries') execute at module-level during import. If pytest imports this file during collection, an assertion failure surfaces as a collection error (not a test failure), which many CI systems report differently. Additionally, wp.init() at line 14 runs at module scope, so importing this file without Warp installed crashes the entire pytest collection.
findings.impact: Kernel coverage failures may be misreported or missed entirely depending on CI pytest configuration. The wp.init() at line 14 makes the file a collection-time landmine on any machine without Warp/CUDA.
findings.fix: Wrap all assertions inside a 'def test_kernel_registry_coverage():' function. Move wp.init() and the imports inside the test function body (or use pytest.importorskip at module level, consistent with test_pressure_projection_regressions.py line 39).

findings.title: 41 of 104 test files have no pytest-discoverable test functions -- entire acceptance/gate test suite is invisible to pytest
findings.description: Systematic analysis shows 41 of 104 test files in tests/ contain zero 'def test_*' functions. These are acceptance/gate/runner scripts designed for 'blender --python' invocation, not pytest. Critical files affected include: blender_memory_safety_gate.py (19 asserts, 0 test functions), blender_capacity_planner_acceptance.py (44 asserts, 0 test functions), blender_whitewater_truth_acceptance.py (18 asserts, 0 test functions), blender_mixed_source_batch_acceptance.py (14 asserts, 0 test functions), blender_gui_acceptance.py (647 lines, 0 test functions), blender_source_sampling_acceptance.py (13 asserts, 0 test functions). Five files (blender_animated_source_acceptance.py, blender_point_source_acceptance.py, blender_source_lifecycle_acceptance.py, blender_source_region_acceptance.py, blender_volume_source_acceptance.py) are 5-line stubs that just call main() from _phase2_source_acceptance_common at module scope.
findings.impact: A 'pytest tests/' run skips the entire acceptance/gate suite silently. Coverage reports will show these files as untested. Developers may believe they have 104 test files when pytest only discovers ~63. The memory safety gate, capacity planner acceptance, and whitewater truth acceptance tests are effectively invisible to standard Python test tooling.
findings.fix: For acceptance tests that must run under Blender: either (a) add a pytest-collectible wrapper that skips when bpy is unavailable and delegates to the acceptance main(), or (b) document a separate test runner and exclude these from the pytest discovery path via pyproject.toml/markers. For the 5-line stub files: their module-scope main() calls execute on import, which is a side effect during pytest collection.

findings.title: smoke_core.py and smoke_solver.py call wp.init() at module scope -- will crash pytest collection without CUDA
findings.description: smoke_core.py lines 3-5: 'import warp as wp / wp.init() / dev = "cuda:0"'. smoke_solver.py lines 9-11: 'import warp as wp / wp.init()'. These execute at import time. When pytest discovers and imports these files during collection (which it will, since they are .py files in tests/), the import will raise if Warp is not installed or CUDA is not available, crashing the entire collection with a hard error rather than a skip. Neither file contains any 'def test_*' function.
findings.impact: Running 'pytest tests/' on any CI machine or developer workstation without CUDA will fail at collection time due to these files, preventing any tests from running at all.
findings.fix: Either move these files outside tests/ (e.g., to a scripts/ or smoke/ directory), or guard the module-level code inside 'if __name__ == "__main__":' blocks and add a pytest skip marker.

findings.title: Production gate tests mock out _run (the core subprocess executor) and all guard functions -- only verifies command assembly, never actual execution
findings.description: Both test_production_gate_semantics.py (_stub_gate at line 18) and test_production_gate_truthfulness.py (fake_run at line 21) monkeypatch _run -- the core subprocess executor of run_production_gate.py -- with a no-op lambda that just records labels. They also stub _check_no_tracked_npz, _check_no_tracked_ignored_files, _clear_gate_manifest, _write_gate_manifest, and _print_gate_metadata. The tests verify that main() assembles the right command labels and output strings, but never verify that any subprocess actually executes, that markers are enforced, or that reject_output scanning works. The production gate is a safety gate -- mocking its execution layer means the tests prove 'the code calls things in the right order' but not 'the things work.'
findings.impact: A regression in _run (subprocess invocation, marker checking, output rejection) would pass all production gate tests while failing in real CI. The gate could silently pass a broken build.
findings.fix: This is partially intentional (you cannot run Blender in unit tests). The gap is that there is no integration test layer that exercises _run with a real subprocess. Add at least one integration test that runs a trivial 'echo MARKER' command through _run and verifies marker enforcement and output rejection end-to-end.

findings.title: Production gate tests mock out _run (the core subprocess executor) and all guard functions -- only verifies command assembly, never actual execution
findings.description: test_memory_safety_recovery.py lines 136-146 read operators.py and panels.py as plain text strings and assert substrings are present: 'assert "bl_idname = \"fluidsim.apply_safe_settings\"" in operators', 'assert "is_memory_capacity_error" in panels'. Line 146 reads run_production_gate.py as text and asserts a filename reference exists. The test itself acknowledges the limitation at line 142-143: 'Limitation: this source-text check proves a live-looking reference, not that the production gate actually executes Blender successfully.' The same pattern appears in tests/test_surface_resolution_feature_contracts.py lines 41 and 130.
findings.impact: These tests pass even if the operator is never registered, the function is dead code, or the reference is in a comment. They provide false confidence that the memory safety recovery UI is wired up correctly.
findings.fix: Replace with import-based checks: import the module and verify the class/function exists as an attribute, verify bpy.types registration via mock. For gate references, verify the string appears in an executable context (not a comment) or better, run the gate with a mock Blender.

findings.title: Mutates sys.modules at import time, deleting all fluidSim_warp_blender51 modules
findings.description: Lines 14-16: 'for _name in list(sys.modules): / if _name == "fluidSim_warp_blender51" or _name.startswith("fluidSim_warp_blender51."): / del sys.modules[_name]'. This runs at module import time. Any test file that imports from _phase2_source_acceptance_common (the 5 stub acceptance files: blender_animated_source_acceptance.py, blender_point_source_acceptance.py, blender_source_lifecycle_acceptance.py, blender_source_region_acceptance.py, blender_volume_source_acceptance.py) triggers this purge. If pytest collects these in the same process as other tests, the module purge can cause other tests to see stale or missing module references.
findings.impact: Test-order-dependent failures in any pytest session that collects both the phase2 stubs and other tests importing fluidSim_warp_blender51 modules. The purge-and-reimport pattern assumes single-process isolation that pytest does not guarantee.
findings.fix: Move the sys.modules purge inside the main() function so it only runs when the acceptance script is explicitly invoked, not during import.

findings.title: No conftest.py anywhere -- cuda_device fixture is defined locally in a single file, no shared fixtures or test isolation configuration
findings.description: No conftest.py exists anywhere in the tests/ directory tree (confirmed: find returned 'no conftest found'). The cuda_device fixture is defined only in tests/test_pressure_projection_regressions.py line 112 as a module-scoped fixture. Every other CUDA test file hardcodes 'cuda:0' and calls wp.init() independently with no shared fixture. There is no shared setUp/teardown for Warp device initialization, no test isolation markers, and no pytest configuration file (no pytest.ini, no pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options]).
findings.impact: Device initialization is duplicated and inconsistent across files (some use wp.init() at module scope, some inside functions, some via pytest.importorskip). Test isolation is unmanaged. Adding a second CUDA device or testing multi-GPU behavior requires touching every file.
findings.fix: Create a tests/conftest.py with a session-scoped cuda_device fixture, standardize Warp initialization, and add pytest markers for CUDA-required vs CPU-only tests.

findings.title: No negative-path tests for solver initialization failure modes (invalid device, capacity overflow during live step, kernel launch failure)
findings.description: The solver has explicit error handling at solver.py:600-630 (invalid device string -> RuntimeError with actionable message, non-CUDA device -> RuntimeError). The pressure solver has launch failure handling at cuda_reduction.py:133 (result != 0 -> RuntimeError). The sourcing module has invariant violation detection at sourcing.py (admitted/emitted count mismatch -> RuntimeError). None of these error paths are tested. While memory_safety_recovery.py tests the classification of error strings (is_memory_capacity_error) and capacity_planner tests capacity BLOCKED verdicts, there are no tests that trigger actual solver initialization failures, live capacity overflow during step_frame(), or kernel launch failures.
findings.impact: The fail-closed error paths in the solver -- which are the last line of defense against silent data corruption -- are untested. A regression in the device validation or capacity guard could go undetected.
findings.fix: Add tests for: FluidSolver.__init__ with invalid device string (expect RuntimeError), FluidSolver.__init__ with non-CUDA device (expect RuntimeError), capacity overflow during step_frame() (expect RuntimeError or safe shutdown), and the sourcing invariant violation path.

findings.title: All CUDA tests hardcode 'cuda:0' with no device parameterization or fallback
findings.description: At least 20 test files hardcode the string 'cuda:0' (smoke_core.py:5, smoke_solver.py:11, _subset_runner.py:26, _phase2_source_acceptance_common.py:53/87/146/564, blender_capacity_planner_acceptance.py:48/70/72, blender_memory_safety_gate.py:33, blender_mixed_source_batch_acceptance.py:43/65/66, blender_topology_transaction_acceptance.py:20-21, blender_whitewater_truth_acceptance.py:165-168, headless_spatiotemporal_validation.py:29, headless_stflip_benchmark.py:217, headless_surface_resolution_pipeline.py:142, test_compiled_source_operations.py:38/56/80, test_device_preference_routing.py:62/66). Only headless_stflip_benchmark.py, headless_spatiotemporal_validation.py, and headless_surface_resolution_pipeline.py accept --device as a CLI argument (but default to cuda:0).
findings.impact: Tests cannot run on multi-GPU systems targeting a specific device, and cannot adapt to environments where cuda:0 is unavailable but cuda:1 is. This limits CI flexibility and hardware test coverage.
findings.fix: Use a shared fixture or environment variable (e.g., FLUIDSIM_TEST_DEVICE) that defaults to cuda:0 but can be overridden. Parameterize the device in tests that use it.
